Local projections

Source: R/lp.R
lp.Rd

Jorda (2005) local projections: for each horizon \(h=0,\dots,H\) and each response \(y_k\), $$y_{k,t+h} = \alpha_h + \beta_h s_t + \gamma_h' w_t + e_{t+h},$$ where \(s_t\) is the shock, \(w_t\) the controls (lags of Y, optional contemporaneous variables, extra controls). \(\beta_h\) is the impulse response at horizon \(h\). The regressions, 2SLS and HAC standard errors run in C++.

lp(
  Y,
  shock,
  horizon = 20L,
  lags = 4L,
  contemp = NULL,
  controls = NULL,
  iv = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  cumulative = NULL,
  se = c("nw", "hc"),
  nw_lag = NULL,
  lag_augment = FALSE,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  dof_adjust = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

numeric matrix / data frame (T x K) of responses (and the source of lag controls).

shock

the shock \(s_t\): a column name/index of Y (observed shock; unit-impact normalisation) or a numeric vector of length T (external shock series, e.g. narrative).

horizon

maximum horizon H.

lags

number of lags of Y in the controls (and of an external shock).

contemp

names/indices of Y columns entered contemporaneously as controls. For a recursive (Cholesky) identification with shock a column of Y, list the variables ordered before the shock.

controls

optional extra T x q matrix of controls.

iv

optional T x q matrix of instruments for shock (LP-IV; Stock & Watson 2018).

responses

subset of Y columns to use as responses (default all).

cumulative

variables whose response is cumulated (\(\sum_{j=0}^h y_{t+j}\)), for variables measured in differences.

se

"nw" Newey-West/Bartlett or "hc" Eicker-Huber-White (HC1).

nw_lag

Newey-West truncation lag; default h + 1.

lag_augment

Montiel Olea & Plagborg-Moller (2021) lag augmentation: add one extra lag that is not interpreted and use "hc" standard errors, valid without stationarity assumptions and robust at long horizons.

level

confidence levels for the pointwise bands.

dof_adjust

apply an n/(n-m) small-sample factor to the Newey-West variance.

Value

an lpm object: $estimate ((H+1) x K), $se, $bands, $nobs.

Examples

fit <- lp(yraw, shock = "V3", horizon = 12, lags = 2, contemp = c("V1", "V2"))
#> Error: unknown shock: V3
fit
#> Error: object 'fit' not found
